paragraphs: On Saturday morning, Mia and I took the bus to the town library. Mia is shy with new people, so I stood next to the driver. "Good morning," said the driver. "Where are you going?" "We are going to the library," I said. "Two return tickets, please."

"That is twenty baht," said the driver. "Do you pay with cash?" "Yes," I said, and I gave him the money. He gave us two small tickets. "Keep them for the way back," he said. Mia smiled at him, but she did not speak, because she was shy.

It was a sunny day, and the road was very busy. We sat near the window, and the bus started. After five minutes, the bus stopped on a busy road. "What is the problem?" asked a woman behind us. "There is a lot of traffic," said the driver. Then we heard a loud noise. An ambulance came down the road with a light on its roof. All the cars moved to the side, and the ambulance passed. A boy in front of us pointed at the light. It went to the hospital near the library.

I thought, "We will miss the first hour at the library." "Is the bus always late?" I asked the driver. "No, it is not," he said. "A normal trip takes fifteen minutes." "Today we are delayed, because all the cars had to wait for the ambulance." "Is it a long wait?" asked Mia. "Only ten more minutes," said the driver. "Thank you," said Mia, and she smiled.

"When do you finish work today?" Mia asked him. "At four o'clock," said the driver. "Then you can take us home!" said Mia. He laughed and said, "Maybe!" I was happy, because Mia was not shy now. The bus arrived at the library at ten past ten, and we were late. But the library was still open, and we had a lot of time. We thanked the driver and got off the bus. We hurried through the library door. Where do you go by bus?
